text:
maya: FYI we've got a customer escalation — sudden billing spike + 504s after they upgraded to the latest Python client.
jonathan: Which customer / SDK version? quick summary pls.
maya: AcmeMetrics, using python-client 0.9.1. They upgraded yesterday after the auto-regenerate CI ran. Errors started ~10m after deploy. They reported duplicate requests (same prompt) and extra tokens billed.
li: Possible double-retry loop in generated client? We recently changed retry middleware placement in the generator template.
sara: TS client used the new template too, right? Any difference observed between TS and Python?
maya: TS looks fine for them, only python shows doubled calls. Attached minimal repro from customer:

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
c = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
# single call expected
resp = c.generate("Summarize the report")
print(resp.text)
```

They captured network logs showing two POSTs within 100ms for the same call id.
jonathan: Do they have a custom transport or are they using default requests/urllib3? any middleware wrapped twice?
maya: Default transport. Stack trace shows retry decorator in generated function plus the client-level retry adapter.
li: That's my hunch — generator added retry wrapper at the operation level in addition to the transport adapter. When transport also retries on idempotent errors we get duplicate upstream charges.
li: snippet from the problematic template we pushed:

```py
def generate(self, prompt: str):
    @retry_on_server_error
    def _call():
        return self._transport.request("POST", "/v1/generate", json={"prompt": prompt})
    return _call()
```

and transport.request already has retry semantics.
jonathan: That explains it. Why didn't tests catch it? CI regen tests only assert compile + basic smoke, not billing-safe semantics.
sara: We should add a small behavioral test to the regen CI that ensures operation-level retries are not present when transport-level retries are enabled. Also add a changelog note about retry placement.
alex: From billing side — we can refund duplicates but need to know the window and affected customers. Maya, please collect request_ids and timestamps.
maya: On it. I asked customer for logs and they sent request_ids: [req_01F..., req_01F...]. Sending now.
jonathan: Immediate mitigation: revert the generator template change that added @retry_on_server_error in operation stubs. Can someone open a hotfix PR to rollback and cut a regen patch?
li: I'll open PR now. PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-gen/pull/742
li: The PR removes the operation-level decorator and adds a comment to the template explaining transport vs operation retry.
jonathan: Can we do a patch release of python-client 0.9.2 with the fix, and coordinate with support to ship to affected customers asap?
li: Yes. Building patch, running unit + regen smoke locally.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started for python-client 0.9.2-patch. canary group: 5% users. CI job: pipeline/clients/python/patch-742 #line 12
maya: I'll tell customer we have a patch rolling and we can issue refunds once we verify affected requests.
alex: Please flag billing cases with tag "duplicate-charge-regeneration" and CC me.
jonathan: Also let's add a quick postmortem checklist item: regen template changes that touch retry/timeout behavior must have a "no-dupe-billing" test in CI before merge.
li: agreed. I'll add the test and link to PR.
maya: thanks team, I'll keep updating thread as customer confirms.
jonathan: Great catch, Maya. :thumbsup:
